fact: ModernGhana says investigative editor Ali Soumana of Le Courrier was jailed in September 2025 after a complaint from the Prime Minister over a customs-fraud report (defamation complaint).
ModernGhana says the BBC was suspended in Niger in December 2024; the document gives no reason for the suspension.

ModernGhana says Soumana Maiga of L'Enquêteur was arrested in April 2024 and charged with harming national defence after his paper reported on Russian listening equipment allegedly installed on state buildings.

ModernGhana says the Ministry of the Interior forced the Maison de la Presse, the umbrella body of journalists' associations, to shut down in January 2024 after it spoke out against post-coup press violations.
ModernGhana says Samira Sabou was detained incommunicado for eight days in September 2023 over reporting deemed likely to disturb public order.
ModernGhana says the signals of RFI and France 24 were cut within a week of the July 2023 coup; the document gives no reason.

Human Rights Watch states that on 30 October 2025 Niamey police arrested six journalists (Moussa Kaka and Abdoul Aziz of Radio Television Saraounia, Ibro Chaibou and Souleymane Brah of Voix du Peuple, Youssouf Seriba of Les Echos du Niger, Oumarou Kane of Le Herisson), three of them held at Kollo prison, and charged all six with complicity in circulating a document likely to disturb public order under the 2019 cybercrime law, apparently over sharing on social media an invitation to a state press conference announcing new mandatory levies for the security-forces solidarity fund.
system: Six Nigerien journalists arrested under the 2019 cybercrime law

fact: Human Rights Watch says lawyer Abrourahamane Lirwana was charged and detained from 21 September 2026 over comments about the army, apparently a 12 September Facebook post, and prosecutors sought five years on 6 October.

Niger's National Communication Observatory (ONC) said on 8 May 2026 it was suspending nine France-based outlets (France 24, RFI, AFP, TV5Monde, Jeune Afrique, Mediapart, TF1 Info, LSI Africa, France Afrique Media) over content it said threatened public order, as reported by CPJ.
CPJ reports the ONC suspended nine outlets from reaching audiences in Niger, with a France 24 channel screen showing 'program blocked'.
